label: Four of six dispatch-audit adapters join the shared relative log constant to a session-relative project directory rather than a repository root, so dispatch records scatter into nested .skilled/logs trees; the observed artifact is specs/system-speckit/047-v4-release-line-research/.skilled/logs/cli-dispatch-audit.log (2179 bytes, runtime claude). The Claude adapter consults the least stable source first (payload.cwd) and the most stable second (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR). OpenCode (findRepoRoot) and dsh (repoRoot) anchor correctly.

The sibling Claude preflight-lint reads the same project directory in the opposite priority order (CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR first, process.cwd fallback) and builds skillsRoot from it for the blocking PreToolUse decision, so the two adapters in one directory disagree on a one-line decision and the preflight degrades to a silent approve when the env var is absent.

A gitignore rule at depth (/*/**/.skilled/logs/) specifically silences nested .skilled/logs trees, which makes the path bug in f-iter018-001 invisible to git and to review instead of preventing it; the observed artifact resolves through this rule and is untracked.

Documentation drift: .skilled/logs/README.md describes one canonical cli-dispatch-audit.log for six writers, and .skilled/hooks/dispatch/README.md claims repo-root anchoring for precisely the one adapter that has it, so the documented inspection recipe returns the last pre-drift record with no signal distinguishing it from 'no dispatches since'.

Improvement: the shared dispatch-audit core should export a rooted resolver (join(findRepoRoot(projectDir), DEFAULT_LOG_RELATIVE_PATH)) instead of letting six adapters each decide, since the core already owns the constant and the OpenCode and dsh adapters already compute a repo root; caveat is that findRepoRoot exists twice at the same signature in shared/workspace and runtime/hooks/lib/workspace and the chosen copy must not drift.

Extension: a doctor or hook-install check that fails when a nested .skilled/logs directory exists outside the root (find . -type d -name logs -path '*/.skilled/logs' -not -path './.skilled/logs') closes this whole class for every future adapter at the cost of one shell line, and nothing in the current doctor surface notices the artifact.

Operator UX: telemetry loss is silent in both directions - the dispatch returns normally, the hook exits 0, and the canonical log simply stops growing with no counter, stderr note or doctor row; the cheapest remedy is a logRootSource field on each record so a drifted write is self-describing on inspection.

Two concerns in this cluster already anchor correctly and supply the fix pattern rather than needing one: goal-core resolves a repo root before building its state dir and goal-slice walks upward testing for .git or .skilled/skills, while decision-capture canonicalises through 'git rev-parse --show-toplevel' with GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE scrubbed and a realpath fallback. Only the dispatch adapters skipped a step the cluster had already solved three ways.

Carried hook-safety question partly closed: the git-call time limit is 5000 ms on decision-capture's rev-parse, cached per distinct input directory so the cost is one subprocess per working directory; the shared stdin reader defaults to 3000 ms with a 64 MiB cap. Both are bounded, retiring the unbounded-hook-stdin worry for adapters that use the shared reader.

The only other .skilled/logs writers in the tree are the shared dispatch-audit core and the codex-hooks-watchdog plugin, so the log surface is small and two writers wide; the fragmentation risk lives in the per-runtime adapters that call the core, not in unexamined extra loggers.
